8-1.bio:
On the first of August the Church enters the Dormition Fast, two weeks of fasting and prayer in preparation for the great feast of the Dormition of the Theotokos on August 15. During these days the faithful gather in the evenings for the Paraklesis, the supplicatory canon to the Mother of God, seeking her intercession.

On this day the Church also keeps the Procession of the Precious Cross, an observance from Constantinople in which the Cross was carried forth for the blessing and protection of the people. The fast begins on August 1.
8-1.desc: Beginning of the Dormition Fast — Procession of the Cross.
8-1.name: Beginning of the Dormition Fast

8-1.bio:
St. Elesa was a virgin martyr honored by tradition as the patroness of the island of Kythira. Her very birth was an answer to prayer: her mother, a pious Christian who had long struggled to bear a child, prayed fervently and received the divine assurance that God had shown her mercy — in Greek, ho Theos elesese — and so the daughter granted to her was named Elesa. Raised by her mother in the faith despite her pagan father, she embraced Christ and consecrated her life to Him. When her father raged against her faith she fled across the water to Kythira; pursuing her there, he put her to death, and she received the crown of martyrdom in her youth.

Because her own birth was God's answer to a childless mother's prayer, St. Elesa is venerated as a protector of childbirth and of expectant mothers, who seek her intercession for the gift of children and a safe delivery. On the mountain of Kythira where tradition places her martyrdom stands the monastery that bears her name, a place of pilgrimage for the islanders. Her feast is celebrated on August 1.
8-1.desc: Holy Virgin-Martyr Elesa, patron saint of Kythira and protector of childbirth and expectant mothers.
8-1.name: Elesa of Kythira

8-1.bio:
On the first of August the Church commemorates the bringing forth of the Precious Cross from the imperial treasury in Constantinople. Tradition relates that the relic was carried through the city during the hot summer weeks to sanctify the streets and to ward off sickness.

The feast is kept with the Lesser Blessing of Waters and marks the beginning of the two-week Dormition Fast.
8-1.desc: Procession of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross, opening the Dormition Fast with the blessing of waters.
8-1.name: Procession of the Precious Cross

8-1.bio:
The Holy Maccabees are the seven brothers who, with their mother Solomone and the aged scribe Eleazar, refused to break the Law of God under the Syrian king Antiochus Epiphanes. Their story is told in the Second Book of Maccabees.

The Church honours them as forerunners of the Christian martyrs, and their mother as an image of steadfast faith who encouraged each of her sons to endure to the end.
8-1.desc: The seven Maccabee brothers, their mother Solomone and their teacher Eleazar, martyred for the Law of God before Christ.
8-1.name: Seven Maccabees, Solomone and Eleazar

8-1.bio:
The Nine Martyrs of Perge were simple working men of Pamphylia who confessed Christ during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that they destroyed a pagan altar and were put to death after refusing to sacrifice.

Their names are preserved in the synaxaria, and they are honoured together on this day.
8-1.desc: Holy Nine Martyrs who suffered at Perge in Pamphylia under Diocletian.
8-1.name: Nine Martyrs of Perge

8-1.bio:
Saint Timothy was archbishop of Proconnesus, an island in the Sea of Marmara. He is remembered as a shepherd of great compassion whose prayers brought healing to the sick.

Tradition relates that he reposed in peace, and the Church calls him Wonderworker because of the many cures worked through him.
8-1.desc: Saint Timothy the Wonderworker, Archbishop of Proconnesus.
8-1.name: Timothy of Proconnesus

8-1.bio:
Venerable Anthony the New was a monk who embraced the ascetic life in the Byzantine period and became known for his humility and gifts of prayer.

The synaxaria remember him as a wonderworker, and he is commemorated on this day together with the other saints of the first of August.
8-1.desc: Venerable Anthony the New, wonderworker and ascetic.
8-1.name: Anthony the New of Constantinople

8-10.bio:
St. Lawrence was archdeacon of the Church of Rome in the third century, entrusted with her treasury and her care for the poor. In the persecution of Valerian, when the prefect demanded the treasures of the Church, Lawrence gathered the poor and the sick and presented them, saying that these were her treasures.

For this he was put to a cruel death by fire in the year 258, enduring, according to tradition, with unbroken and even joyful courage. His martyrdom is honored in both East and West, and he is commemorated on August 10.
8-10.name: Lawrence the Archdeacon

8-10.bio:
Saint Sixtus was bishop of Rome during the persecution of Valerian and was beheaded in 258, a few days before his archdeacon Lawrence. Hippolytus, a soldier who guarded Lawrence, was moved by his faith to become a Christian and was himself martyred.

They are commemorated together with Saint Lawrence on this day.
8-10.desc: Hieromartyr Sixtus, Pope of Rome, with the Martyr Hippolytus, companions of the Archdeacon Lawrence.
8-10.name: Sixtus of Rome and Hippolytus

8-10.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Heron was a philosopher who embraced Christ and confessed Him before the pagans, for which he was put to death.

He is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-10.name: Heron the Philosopher

8-10.bio:
The Six Martyrs of Bizye confessed Christ in the Thracian city of Bizye during the pagan persecutions and were put to death together.

Their names are not preserved; they are honoured as a company.
8-10.desc: Holy Six Martyrs who suffered at Bizye in Thrace.
8-10.name: Six Martyrs of Bizye

8-10.bio:
Saint Agathonike was a Christian virgin of Carthage in North Africa who refused to sacrifice to idols and was put to death for her faith.

She is remembered among the virgin martyrs of the early Church.
8-10.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Agathonike, who suffered at Carthage.
8-10.name: Agathonike of Carthage

8-10.bio:
Blessed Lawrence lived in Kaluga in Russia in the early sixteenth century as a fool-for-Christ, going barefoot in winter and summer. Tradition relates that his prayers helped the city withstand a Tatar attack.

He reposed in 1515 and a monastery was later founded at the place of his ascetic struggles.
8-10.name: Lawrence of Kaluga

8-11.bio:
St. Euphrosyne of Alexandria was the only daughter of a wealthy and devout father in the fifth century. Desiring the monastic life and fleeing an arranged marriage, she secretly left her home and, concealing her identity in a men's monastery, spent many years in prayer, fasting, and hidden struggle.

Near the end of her life she was revealed to her own father, who had long mourned her, and who himself then took up the monastic life in her cell. She is commemorated on August 11.
8-11.name: Euphrosyne

8-11.bio:
Saint Euplos was a deacon in Catania in Sicily during the persecution of Diocletian. He was arrested while carrying the book of the Gospels and, refusing to surrender it or to deny Christ, was tortured and beheaded in 304.

He is honoured as one of the great martyrs of Sicily.
8-11.desc: Holy Great Martyr Euplos the Deacon of Catania.
8-11.name: Euplos the Deacon

8-11.bio:
Saint Niphon was a monk of Mount Athos who was twice raised to the patriarchal throne of Constantinople in the late fifteenth century. Deposed by the Ottomans, he served the Church in Wallachia and later returned to the Monastery of Dionysiou, where he lived humbly as a simple monk.

His relics rest at Dionysiou, and he is greatly venerated in both Greece and Romania.
8-11.desc: Saint Niphon, Patriarch of Constantinople and ascetic of Mount Athos.
8-11.name: Niphon Patriarch of Constantinople

8-11.bio:
Saints Anastasios and Demetrios were young men from the island of Lesvos who were pressured to convert to Islam. Repenting of a moment of weakness, they confessed Christ before the Ottoman authorities in Mytilene and were put to death in the nineteenth century.

They are honoured among the New Martyrs of Lesvos.
8-11.desc: Holy New Martyrs Anastasios Paneras and Demetrios Begiazis of Lesvos.
8-11.name: Anastasios and Demetrios of Lesvos

8-11.bio:
The synaxaria record that these six martyrs confessed Christ and were put to death together for their faith.

They are commemorated as a company on this day.
8-11.desc: Holy Martyrs Neophytos, Zenon, Gaios, Markos, Makarios and Gaianos.
8-11.greek: Νεόφυτος, Ζήνων, Γάιος, Μάρκος, Μακάριος και Γαϊανός
8-11.name: Neophytos, Zenon and Companions

8-12.bio:
Sts. Photius and Anicetas were martyrs of Nicomedia who suffered during the persecution of Diocletian at the beginning of the fourth century. According to tradition they were kinsmen; Anicetas confessed Christ boldly before the emperor, and Photius embraced him and followed him in his confession. Together they endured imprisonment and many torments, and were finally put to death by fire, receiving together the crown of martyrdom.

Their shared steadfastness has been honored through the centuries, and those named Photios and Fotis keep their name day in their memory. They are commemorated on August 12.
8-12.desc: Holy Martyrs Photius and Anicetas of Nicomedia.
8-12.name: Martyrs Photius & Anicetas

8-12.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saints Pamphilos and Kapiton confessed Christ and were beheaded for their faith.

They are commemorated together on this day.
8-12.name: Pamphilos and Kapiton

8-12.bio:
Saint Palamon was a hermit of the Egyptian Thebaid in the fourth century, known for his severe asceticism. He received the young Pachomios as his disciple and trained him in the monastic life.

He reposed in peace, and through his disciple he stands at the root of cenobitic monasticism.
8-12.desc: Venerable Palamon, teacher of Saint Pachomios the Great.
8-12.name: Palamon the Ascetic

8-12.bio:
The Twelve Soldier Martyrs were Cretan soldiers who confessed Christ and were beheaded together.

They are honoured as a company on this day.
8-12.desc: Holy Twelve Soldier Martyrs from Crete, beheaded for Christ.
8-12.name: Twelve Soldier Martyrs of Crete

8-12.bio:
Saint Kastor was an ascetic who lived in prayer and stillness and reposed in peace.

Little more is preserved of his life.
8-12.desc: Venerable Kastor, who reposed in peace.
8-12.name: Kastor the Ascetic

8-13.bio:
St. Maximos the Confessor was a monk and theologian of the seventh century. Leaving high office in Constantinople for the monastic life, he became the great defender of the true faith against monothelitism, teaching that Christ, being true God and true man, possesses both a divine and a human will. For refusing to keep silence he was tried, mutilated, and exiled, dying in banishment in 662.

His profound writings on theology and the spiritual life remain treasures of the Church. His principal feast is January 21; on August 13 the Church commemorates the translation of his relics.
8-13.name: Maximos the Confessor

8-13.bio:
Saint Eudokia was born Athenais, daughter of an Athenian philosopher, and after her baptism married the Emperor Theodosius II. A woman of learning and piety, she composed verse on Scripture and built churches and hospices in Jerusalem.

She spent her last years in the Holy City and reposed there in the fifth century.
8-13.desc: Righteous Eudokia, Empress, wife of Theodosius the Younger.
8-13.name: Eudokia the Empress

8-13.bio:
Saint Dorotheos was a monk of the monastery of Abba Seridos near Gaza in the sixth century and a disciple of the great elders Barsanuphios and John. He later founded his own monastery and wrote instructions on the spiritual life that remain among the most read works of Orthodox monasticism.

His teaching stresses humility, obedience and the cutting off of self-will.
8-13.desc: Venerable Dorotheos of Gaza, abbot and spiritual teacher.
8-13.name: Dorotheos of Gaza

8-13.bio:
Saint Dositheos was a young man of noble family who entered the monastery near Gaza under the care of Saint Dorotheos. Though weak in body and unable to keep the ascetic rule, he attained holiness in a few years through perfect obedience and the cutting off of his own will.

His brief life is told in the writings of his teacher.
8-13.desc: Venerable Dositheos, disciple of Saint Dorotheos of Gaza.
8-13.name: Dositheos of Gaza

8-13.bio:
Saint Irene was a Hungarian princess who married the Emperor John II Komnenos. She was known for her charity and founded the great Monastery of Christ Pantokrator in Constantinople with its hospital for the poor.

Before her death in the twelfth century she received the monastic habit under the name Xene.
8-13.desc: Righteous Irene the Empress, wife of John II Komnenos, the nun Xene.
8-13.name: Irene the Empress (Xene)

8-13.bio:
Saint Tikhon was Bishop of Voronezh in the eighteenth century and, after retiring for reasons of health, lived at the Zadonsk monastery. There he wrote spiritual works, received visitors of every rank and gave generously to the poor.

He reposed in 1783 and is one of the most beloved saints of the Russian Church.
8-13.desc: Saint Tikhon, Bishop of Voronezh and wonderworker of Zadonsk.
8-13.name: Tikhon of Zadonsk

8-14.bio:
The Holy Prophet Micah was one of the twelve minor prophets, prophesying in the kingdom of Judah in the eighth century before Christ, in the days of the Prophet Isaiah. He rebuked injustice and false worship, foretold judgment upon Jerusalem, and proclaimed the mercy of God who pardons iniquity.

Above all he is remembered for foretelling that from Bethlehem would come forth the Ruler of Israel, the prophecy fulfilled in the Nativity of Christ. He is commemorated on August 14.
8-14.name: Micah the Prophet

8-14.bio:
Saint Markellos was bishop of Apamea in Syria in the fourth century. Tradition relates that while overseeing the destruction of a pagan temple he was seized by pagans and burned to death.

He is honoured as a hieromartyr.
8-14.desc: Hieromartyr Markellos, Bishop of Apamea in Syria.
8-14.name: Markellos of Apamea

8-14.bio:
Saint Symeon was a goldsmith from Trebizond who lived and worked in Constantinople. Accused of blasphemy against Islam, he refused to save himself by conversion and was burned to death in the seventeenth century.

He is honoured among the New Martyrs.
8-14.desc: Holy New Martyr Symeon the Goldsmith of Trebizond.
8-14.name: Symeon of Trebizond

8-14.bio:
Saint Oursikios was an officer from Illyria in the Roman army who confessed Christ before the Emperor Maximian. After tortures he was beheaded.

He is commemorated among the martyrs of this day.
8-14.desc: Holy Martyr Oursikios, a military officer who suffered under Maximian.
8-14.name: Oursikios the Martyr

8-14.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Lucius was a soldier who confessed Christ and was put to death for his faith.

He is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-14.name: Lucius the Soldier

8-15.bio:
The Great Feast of the Dormition commemorates the falling asleep of the Most Holy Theotokos. According to tradition, the Apostles were gathered from the ends of the earth to her bedside in Jerusalem, where she gave her soul into the hands of her Son; her body was laid in a tomb in Gethsemane and was found to have been taken up, for the Mother of Life was translated to life.

Kept on August 15 at the close of the two-week Dormition Fast, this is the greatest of the feasts of the Theotokos — the Pascha of summer, as it is called in Greek tradition — and the name day of Maria, Panagiota, and Despina.
8-15.desc: The Dormition (Falling Asleep) of our Most Holy Lady the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary.
8-15.name: Dormition of the Theotokos

8-15.bio:
Saint Tarcisius was a young acolyte of the Church of Rome in the third century. Tradition relates that while carrying the Holy Eucharist to imprisoned Christians he was set upon by a pagan mob and beaten to death rather than surrender the Holy Gifts.

He is honoured as a martyr of the Eucharist.
8-15.desc: Holy Martyr Tarcisius, the young acolyte who died protecting the Holy Gifts.
8-15.name: Tarcisius of Rome

8-16.bio:
This feast commemorates the translation of the Holy Mandylion, the Icon of Christ Not-Made-by-Hands, from Edessa to Constantinople in the tenth century. According to tradition, King Abgar of Edessa, suffering from illness, sent to the Lord asking for healing, and received a cloth upon which the face of Christ had been imprinted without human hands; through it he was healed and believed.

The Mandylion was treasured in Edessa for centuries and brought with great honor to Constantinople on August 16. The feast celebrates Christ as the true image of God made visible in the flesh, and stands at the foundation of the Orthodox veneration of icons.
8-16.desc: Translation of the Not-Made-by-Hands Icon (Mandylion) to Constantinople.
8-16.name: Translation of Mandylion

8-16.bio:
Saint Diomedes was a physician from Tarsus in Cilicia who healed both bodies and souls, bringing many to Christ. He settled in Nicaea, where he was arrested under Diocletian and died on the way to trial.

Tradition relates that the soldiers who beheaded his body were struck blind and healed only when they returned his head to it.
8-16.desc: Holy Martyr Diomedes the Unmercenary Physician of Tarsus.
8-16.name: Diomedes the Physician

8-16.bio:
Saint Stamatios was a young man from the region of Volos who went to Constantinople to protest the oppression of his village by Ottoman officials. Arrested and urged to convert, he confessed Christ steadfastly and was beheaded in 1680.

He is the patron of all who bear his name.
8-16.desc: Holy New Martyr Stamatios of Volos, beheaded at Constantinople.
8-16.name: Stamatios of Volos

8-16.bio:
Saint Apostolos was born in the village of Agios Lavrentios on Mount Pelion and worked in Constantinople. Slandered before the authorities, he refused to deny Christ and was beheaded in the seventeenth century.

He is honoured especially in Thessaly and by those who bear his name.
8-16.desc: Holy New Martyr Apostolos of Agios Lavrentios on Mount Pelion.
8-16.name: Apostolos the New

8-16.bio:
Saint Joseph was born on the island of Paros and went to Mount Athos as a young man, where he lived in caves and huts of extreme austerity, devoting himself to the Jesus Prayer. His disciples went on to renew several Athonite monasteries and to found communities across the world.

He reposed on the feast of the Dormition in 1959 and was numbered among the saints in 2020.
8-16.desc: Venerable Joseph the Hesychast, the Cave-Dweller of Mount Athos.
8-16.name: Joseph the Hesychast

8-16.bio:
Saint Gerasimos was born in the Peloponnese in the sixteenth century, became a monk on Mount Athos and later settled on Cephalonia, where he founded a convent at Omala and served the people in famine and sickness. He reposed on the fifteenth of August 1579.

His relics remain incorrupt, and the island keeps his feast both on this day and on the twentieth of October.
8-16.desc: Venerable Gerasimos the New Ascetic, protector of Cephalonia, remembered on the day of his repose.
8-16.name: Gerasimos of Cephalonia (Repose)

8-16.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Alkiviades confessed Christ and was burned alive for his faith.

He is honoured on this day and is the patron of those who bear his name.
8-16.desc: Holy Martyr Alkiviades, who was burned for Christ.
8-16.name: Alkiviades the Martyr

8-17.bio:
St. Myron was a presbyter of Cyzicus in Asia Minor who lived in the middle of the third century. Tradition relates that when the governor Antipater burst into the church during the Nativity service, Myron rebuked him openly and was seized, tortured, and cast to wild beasts, which left him unharmed.

He was at length beheaded for his confession of Christ. The Church honors him as a hieromartyr and commemorates him on August 17. (The wonderworking Bishop Myron of Crete, famed for his kindness to thieves in his threshing floor, is kept on August 8.)
8-17.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Myron, presbyter of Cyzicus.
8-17.name: Myron of Cyzicus

8-17.bio:
These four martyrs preached Christ to the crowds at the theatre of Nicomedia and drew many away from pagan spectacles. Arrested by the governor, they refused to sacrifice and were thrown to wild beasts and then burned.

They are commemorated together on this day.
8-17.desc: Holy Martyrs Straton, Philip, Eutychianos and Kyprianos of Nicomedia.
8-17.name: Straton, Philip, Eutychianos and Kyprianos

8-17.bio:
Saint Demetrios was a monk from Samarina in the Pindos mountains who preached to the villagers of Epirus. Suspected of stirring resistance, he was seized by the men of Ali Pasha and tortured to death in Ioannina in 1808.

He is honoured among the New Martyrs of Epirus.
8-17.desc: Holy New Martyr Demetrios the Monk of Samarina in Pindos.
8-17.name: Demetrios of Samarina

8-17.bio:
Saints Paul and Juliana were brother and sister from Ptolemais in Phoenicia who confessed Christ before the Emperor Aurelian. Their endurance under torture moved several of their guards to believe, and these were martyred with them.

They were beheaded in the third century.
8-17.desc: Holy Martyrs Paul and his sister Juliana, with those who suffered with them.
8-17.name: Paul and Juliana of Ptolemais

8-17.bio:
Saint Alypios was a monk of the Kiev Caves Monastery in the eleventh century and one of the first iconographers of Rus. He painted without payment, gave his earnings to the poor and, tradition relates, healed the sick by anointing them with the colours of his palette.

He is honoured as the patron of iconographers.
8-17.desc: Venerable Alypios the Iconographer of the Kiev Caves.
8-17.name: Alypios the Iconographer

8-17.bio:
Saints Thyrsos, Leukios and Koronatos suffered with their companions at Caesarea in Bithynia during the persecution of Decius.

Their principal feast is in December; they are remembered again on this day.
8-17.desc: Holy Martyrs Thyrsos, Leukios, Koronatos and their companions.
8-17.name: Thyrsos, Leukios and Koronatos

8-18.bio:
Sts. Floros and Lavros were brothers, stonemasons by trade, who labored in Illyricum in the early centuries of the Church. Hired to build a pagan temple, they gave their wages to the poor, and when the work was done they gathered the poor together, overturned the idols, and consecrated the building to Christ. For this they were put to death, according to tradition cast into a well.

Their memory has been kept with love among the Orthodox peoples, and in Slavic tradition they are honored as protectors of horses. They are commemorated on August 18.
8-18.name: Floros and Lavros

8-18.bio:
Saint Arsenios was born in Ioannina in 1800 and became a disciple of Saint Gregory of Paros. He served as spiritual father of the Convent of the Transfiguration on Paros, where he was renowned for his gifts of prayer and discernment.

He reposed in 1877; this day marks the uncovering of his relics, and his principal feast is on the thirty-first of January.
8-18.desc: Venerable Arsenios the New of Paros, remembered on the translation of his relics.
8-18.name: Arsenios of Paros

8-18.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saints Hermes, Serapion and Polyainos confessed Christ at Rome and were dragged over rough ground until they died.

They are commemorated together on this day.
8-18.desc: Holy Martyrs Hermes, Serapion and Polyainos of Rome.
8-18.name: Hermes, Serapion and Polyainos

8-18.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Juliana confessed Christ and was put to death near Strobilos.

She is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-18.desc: Holy Martyr Juliana, who suffered near Strobilos.
8-18.name: Juliana of Strobilos

8-18.bio:
Saints John and George were successive patriarchs of Constantinople in the reign of Constantine Pogonatos. George presided during the Sixth Ecumenical Council, which condemned the Monothelite heresy.

They reposed in peace and are commemorated together.
8-18.desc: Saints George and John, Patriarchs of Constantinople in the seventh century.
8-18.name: George and John, Patriarchs of Constantinople

8-18.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Leo confessed Christ and was drowned in the sea for his faith.

He is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-18.desc: Holy Martyr Leo, who was cast into the sea.
8-18.name: Leo the Martyr

8-18.bio:
Saint Sophronios lived as a monk in the Skete of Saint Anne on Mount Athos in the eighteenth century, spending many decades in obedience and prayer.

He reposed in peace and is honoured among the Athonite fathers.
8-18.desc: Venerable Sophronios of the Skete of Saint Anne on Mount Athos.
8-18.name: Sophronios the Athonite

8-19.bio:
St. Andrew Stratelates was a commander in the Roman army in the East at the end of the third century. Calling on the name of Christ, he led his soldiers to victory, and confessed openly the faith that had given it; many of his men believed with him and were baptized.

Denounced during the persecution of Maximian, he and a great company of his fellow soldiers withdrew to the mountains of Cilicia, where they were overtaken and slain, receiving together the crown of martyrdom. He is commemorated on August 19.
8-19.name: Andrew the General

8-19.bio:
Saint Theophanes was born in Ioannina and became a monk on Mount Athos, where he served as abbot of Docheiariou. He later settled near Naousa in Macedonia and founded a monastery there.

He reposed in the sixteenth century and is the patron saint of Naousa.
8-19.desc: Venerable Theophanes the New, wonderworker of Naousa in Macedonia.
8-19.name: Theophanes the New of Naousa

8-19.bio:
Saints Timothy, Agapios and Thekla suffered at Gaza and Caesarea in Palestine during the persecution of Diocletian. Timothy was burned, while Agapios and Thekla were thrown to wild beasts.

They are commemorated together on this day.
8-19.desc: Holy Martyrs Timothy, Agapios and Thekla of Palestine.
8-19.name: Timothy, Agapios and Thekla

8-19.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Eutychianos, a soldier, and Saint Stratigios confessed Christ and were burned for their faith.

They are commemorated together on this day.
8-19.desc: Holy Martyrs Eutychianos the Soldier and Stratigios.
8-19.name: Eutychianos and Stratigios

8-19.bio:
Saint Gennadios was a Lithuanian-born monk of sixteenth-century Russia who became a disciple of Saint Cornelius of Komel and founded a monastery near Kostroma.

He was known for his labours and his gift of foresight and reposed in 1565.
8-19.desc: Venerable Gennadios of Kostroma and Lubimograd.
8-19.name: Gennadios of Kostroma

8-2.bio:
This feast commemorates the translation of the relics of the Holy Protomartyr and Archdeacon Stephen, the first to shed his blood for Christ, stoned outside Jerusalem as recorded in the Acts of the Apostles. According to tradition, his long-hidden relics were revealed in the fifth century and were later brought with great honor to Constantinople, where the faithful received them with rejoicing.

Through his relics many healings were granted, and the Church glorifies God who is wondrous in His saints. The translation is commemorated on August 2; his principal feast is December 27.
8-2.desc: Translation of the relics of the Holy Protomartyr Stephen.
8-2.name: Translation of Relics of St. Stephen

8-2.bio:
Saint Theodore was a Greek Christian who, in the years of Ottoman rule, was pressured to renounce his faith. Tradition relates that after a period of weakness he repented openly, confessed Christ before the authorities at the Dardanelles and was put to death.

He is one of the many New Martyrs of the Turkish yoke honoured by the Greek Church.
8-2.desc: Holy New Martyr Theodore, who suffered at the Dardanelles under the Ottomans.
8-2.name: Theodore the New Martyr of Dardanelles

8-2.bio:
Venerable Photeine lived as a hermitess in a cave near Rizokarpaso in Cyprus. Tradition relates that she spent her life in prayer and fasting, and that the faithful of the region venerated her from an early date.

A church and holy spring in the Karpasia peninsula still bear her name.
8-2.desc: Venerable Photeine the Cypriot, ascetic of the Karpasia peninsula.
8-2.name: Photeine of Cyprus

8-2.bio:
Saint Basil the Blessed was a fool-for-Christ who lived in Moscow in the sixteenth century. He went barefoot and half-naked in all seasons, rebuked the powerful without fear and showed compassion to the poor.

He was greatly revered even by Tsar Ivan the Terrible, and the famous cathedral on Red Square bears his name.
8-2.desc: Blessed Basil, Fool-for-Christ and wonderworker of Moscow.
8-2.name: Basil the Blessed of Moscow

8-2.bio:
The Martyrs Maximos, Dadas and Quintilian suffered in Dorostolon in the region of the Danube during the persecution of Diocletian. Their principal feast is in April; on this day the Church remembers the finding of their relics.

The synaxaria record that they were beheaded after refusing to offer sacrifice to idols.
8-2.desc: Holy Martyrs Maximos, Dadas and Quintilian, whose relics were found on this day.
8-2.name: Maximos, Dadas and Quintilian

8-20.bio:
The Holy Prophet Samuel was the last of the judges of Israel, born in answer to the prayers of his mother Hannah, who dedicated him to God from childhood. Serving in the sanctuary at Shiloh, he heard the call of the Lord as a boy, and grew to be a faithful prophet, judging Israel in righteousness.

At God's command he anointed Saul as the first king of Israel, and afterward David, the ancestor of Christ according to the flesh. He reposed in peace and is commemorated on August 20.
8-20.name: Samuel the Prophet

8-20.bio:
Saint Theocharis was a young Greek of Neapolis in Cappadocia, an orphan raised in piety. Seized by the Ottomans and pressed to convert, he refused steadfastly and was put to death in the eighteenth century.

He is honoured especially by the Cappadocian Greeks and by those who bear his name.
8-20.desc: Holy New Martyr Theocharis of Neapolis in Cappadocia.
8-20.name: Theocharis of Neapolis

8-20.bio:
Saints Heliodoros and Dosas were Christians of Persia who confessed Christ under King Shapur and were put to death in the fourth century.

They are commemorated together on this day.
8-20.desc: Holy Martyrs Heliodoros and Dosas, who suffered in Persia.
8-20.name: Heliodoros and Dosas

8-20.bio:
Saints Rheginos and Orestes were martyred in Cyprus for their faith in Christ. Their relics were venerated at Phasoula near Limassol, where a church bears their names.

They are honoured among the saints of Cyprus.
8-20.desc: Holy Martyrs Rheginos and Orestes, who suffered in Cyprus.
8-20.name: Rheginos and Orestes of Cyprus

8-20.bio:
Saint Severus was a Christian of Thrace who confessed Christ under Diocletian. The centurion Memnon, moved by his courage, believed with thirty-seven of his soldiers, and all were put to death together at Bizye.

They are commemorated as a company on this day.
8-20.desc: Holy Martyrs Severus, Memnon the Centurion and thirty-seven soldiers who suffered in Thrace.
8-20.name: Severus, Memnon and the 37 Martyrs of Bizye

8-20.bio:
Saint Lucius was a senator of Cyrene who confessed Christ and was beheaded for his faith in the early fourth century.

He is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-20.desc: Holy Martyr Lucius the Senator, beheaded for Christ.
8-20.name: Lucius the Senator

8-21.bio:
St. Thaddaeus, numbered among the Seventy Apostles, was a Jew of Edessa who came to Jerusalem, heard the preaching of John the Forerunner, and became a disciple of the Lord. According to the ancient tradition of the Church, after Pentecost he was sent to Edessa, where he healed the ruler Abgar, preached the Gospel, and established the Church in that city.

Having enlightened many in Mesopotamia, he completed his apostolic labors in peace. He is commemorated on August 21.
8-21.name: Thaddaeus the Apostle

8-21.bio:
Saint Bassa was the wife of a pagan priest in Edessa who raised her three sons as Christians. Denounced by her husband, she watched her sons die for Christ and then suffered many tortures herself before being beheaded in the reign of Maximian.

She and her sons are honoured together on this day.
8-21.desc: Holy Martyr Bassa of Edessa and her sons Theognios, Agapios and Pistos.
8-21.name: Bassa and her Children

8-21.bio:
Saint Athanasios was born in Crete and twice served briefly as Patriarch of Constantinople in the seventeenth century. Travelling in Russia to seek help for the Church, he reposed at Lubny in Ukraine in 1654.

His relics were found incorrupt, seated in a chair as he had been buried, and he is venerated in both Greece and Russia.
8-21.desc: Saint Athanasios Patellarios, Patriarch of Constantinople, wonderworker of Lubny.
8-21.name: Athanasios Patellarios

8-21.bio:
Saint Alexander was an ascetic who lived in Iconium in Asia Minor and reposed in peace.

Little more is preserved of his life.
8-21.name: Alexander of Iconium

8-21.bio:
Saint Abramios was a monk and preacher of Smolensk in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, learned in the Scriptures and a painter of icons. Slandered and tried by his enemies, he was vindicated and made archimandrite of a monastery in the city.

He reposed in peace and is honoured as a wonderworker.
8-21.desc: Venerable Abramios, Archimandrite of Smolensk, wonderworker.
8-21.name: Abramios of Smolensk

8-22.bio:
St. Phokas served as bishop of Sinope on the Black Sea in the early centuries of the Church, shepherding his flock with holiness during the age of persecutions. Remaining faithful to Christ, he was put to death for his confession and is honored as a hieromartyr.

From ancient times he has been venerated as a protector of those who sail the seas, and churches along the coasts were dedicated to his name. In addition to his principal feast in September, his memory is also kept on August 22.
8-22.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Phocas, Bishop of Sinope.
8-22.name: Phokas of Sinope (Bishop)

8-22.bio:
St. Agathonikos was a Christian of noble birth in Nicomedia who lived in the time of the Emperor Maximian. Zealous for the faith, he brought many pagans to Christ, for which he was seized by the governor, tortured, and taken in chains along the road toward Byzantium together with other confessors.

The synaxaria relate that he and his companions were beheaded for Christ near Selymbria in Thrace. A church was later raised in his honor in Constantinople. He is commemorated on August 22.
8-22.desc: Holy Martyr Agathonikos of Nicomedia and those with him.
8-22.name: Agathonikos of Nicomedia

8-22.bio:
Saint Anthousa was the daughter of pagan parents in Seleucia of Syria who sought out the bishop Athanasios and was baptized by him. She lived thereafter as an ascetic in the wilderness for many years, while Athanasios and her two servants Charisimos and Neophytos were martyred under Valerian.

She reposed in peace and is the patron of those who bear her name.
8-22.desc: Venerable Anthousa of Seleucia, with the Hieromartyr Athanasios who baptized her and her servants Charisimos and Neophytos.
8-22.name: Anthousa of Seleucia

8-22.bio:
Saint Ariadne was the daughter of Emperor Leo I and wife of the Emperors Zeno and Anastasios. She was known for her piety and works of charity in the capital.

She reposed in peace in the early sixth century.
8-22.name: Ariadne the Empress

8-22.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saints Irenaeus, Or and Oropsis confessed Christ and were put to death for their faith.

They are commemorated together on this day.
8-22.desc: Holy Martyrs Irenaeus, Or and Oropsis.
8-22.name: Irenaeus, Or and Oropsis

8-23.bio:
St. Lupus was, according to tradition, the faithful servant of the Great Martyr Demetrios of Thessaloniki. Present at his master's martyrdom at the beginning of the fourth century, he reverently kept relics of the saint, through which God worked healings among the faithful of the city.

When this became known he was seized, and confessing Christ openly he was put to death, following his master in martyrdom. He is commemorated on August 23.
8-23.name: Lupus the Martyr

8-23.bio:
Saint Irenaeus was born in Smyrna and heard Saint Polycarp in his youth. He became bishop of Lyons in Gaul, where he wrote his great work Against Heresies in defence of the apostolic faith and worked for peace between the churches.

Tradition relates that he was martyred with many of his flock in the persecution of Septimius Severus.
8-23.desc: Hieromartyr Irenaeus, Bishop of Lyons, disciple of Saint Polycarp.
8-23.name: Irenaeus of Lyons

8-23.bio:
Saint Kallinikos was Patriarch of Constantinople at the end of the seventh century. He refused the demand of the Emperor Justinian II to bless the demolition of a church and was later blinded and exiled to Rome by the same emperor.

He reposed in exile and is honoured as a confessor.
8-23.desc: Saint Kallinikos, Patriarch of Constantinople and confessor.
8-23.name: Kallinikos Patriarch of Constantinople

8-23.bio:
Saint Irenaeus was bishop of Sirmium in Pannonia. Arrested in the persecution of Diocletian, he refused to sacrifice despite the pleas of his family and was beheaded and cast into the river.

He is commemorated with the other Irenaeus on this day.
8-23.name: Irenaeus of Sirmium

8-23.bio:
Saint Nicholas came from Sicily and lived as a hermit on Mount Neotakos in Euboea, where he was known for his ascetic life and prayer.

He reposed in peace and is venerated on the island of Euboea.
8-23.desc: Venerable Nicholas the Sicilian, ascetic of Mount Neotakos in Euboea.
8-23.name: Nicholas the Sicilian

8-23.bio:
The synaxaria record that thirty-eight Christians confessed Christ in Thrace and were put to death by the sword.

They are honoured together as a company.
8-23.desc: Holy Thirty-Eight Martyrs who suffered in Thrace.
8-23.name: Thirty-Eight Martyrs of Thrace

8-24.bio:
St. Eutyches was a disciple of the apostolic age, remembered by tradition as a follower of St. John the Theologian who also accompanied St. Paul in his labors for the Gospel. Preaching Christ in various lands, he endured imprisonment and torments for the faith.

Though not numbered among the Seventy, he is honored with the title of apostle for his share in their work of evangelization, and he completed his course as a martyr. He is commemorated on August 24.
8-24.name: Eutyches the Apostle

8-24.bio:
Saint Kosmas was born in Aitolia in 1714 and became a monk of Philotheou on Mount Athos. With the blessing of the Patriarch he travelled through Greece, Epirus and Albania for many years, preaching to the enslaved people, founding schools and calling the faithful back to the Gospel.

He was hanged by the Ottomans in 1779 and is honoured as an Equal-to-the-Apostles and teacher of the nation.
8-24.desc: Hieromartyr Kosmas of Aitolia, Equal-to-the-Apostles, preacher of enslaved Greece.
8-24.name: Kosmas of Aitolia

8-24.bio:
Saint Dionysios was born on Zakynthos in the sixteenth century, served briefly as Archbishop of Aegina and returned to his island to live as a monk. He is famed for forgiving and sheltering the man who had killed his brother.

His relics remain incorrupt on Zakynthos; this day marks their translation, and his principal feast is on the seventeenth of December.
8-24.desc: Saint Dionysios of Zakynthos, Archbishop of Aegina, remembered on the translation of his relics.
8-24.name: Dionysios of Zakynthos (Relics)

8-24.bio:
Saint Tation was a Christian of Claudiopolis in Bithynia who confessed Christ during the persecution of Diocletian. After tortures he was dragged through the city and gave up his soul to God.

He is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-24.name: Tation the Martyr

8-24.bio:
Saint George was an aged monk of Mount Olympus in Bithynia who defended the veneration of the holy icons under the iconoclast emperor Leo the Isaurian. He was tortured and had his nose cut off for his confession.

He reposed in peace and is honoured as a confessor.
8-24.desc: Venerable George Limniotes, confessor for the holy icons.
8-24.name: George the Confessor of Lake

8-25.bio:
This feast commemorates the translation of the relics of the Holy Apostle Bartholomew, one of the Twelve, who preached the Gospel in eastern lands and completed his apostolic course as a martyr. According to tradition, his relics, placed in a coffin and cast into the sea by persecutors, were carried by the waves and received with honor by the faithful, coming at last to the island of Lipari.

The Church glorifies God who preserves the relics of His apostles as wellsprings of blessing. The translation is commemorated on August 25, alongside his principal feast on June 11.
8-25.desc: Transfer of Relics of Holy Apostle Bartholomew.
8-25.name: Return of the Relics of Bartholomew

8-25.bio:
St. Chrysostomos the New, Metropolitan of Florina, was a hierarch and confessor of the twentieth century. A learned and ascetic bishop, he took up the leadership of the Genuine Orthodox Christians of Greece who held to the traditional church calendar, and for this confession he endured deprivation, censure, and exile, bearing all with patience and meekness.

He reposed in 1955, revered by his flock as a confessor of the faith. His memory is honored on August 25, and he is invoked as an intercessor by those who cherish the traditions of the fathers.
8-25.desc: St. Chrysostomos the New, Confessor and Metropolitan of Florina, hierarch of the Genuine Orthodox Church.
8-25.name: Chrysostomos the New of Florina

8-25.bio:
Saint Titus was a native of Crete and a disciple and companion of the Apostle Paul, who addressed to him one of the Pastoral Epistles. Paul left him in Crete to organize the Church there, and he became its first bishop.

He reposed in old age at Gortyna and is the patron saint of Crete.
8-25.desc: Holy Apostle Titus of the Seventy, first Bishop of Crete.
8-25.name: Titus the Apostle

8-25.bio:
Saint John came from the island of Karpathos and lived the monastic life, leaving writings of counsel to monks that were later included in the Philokalia.

He reposed in peace and is honoured among the fathers of the spiritual life.
8-25.desc: Venerable John of Karpathos, ascetic and spiritual writer.
8-25.name: John the Karpathian

8-25.bio:
Saint John the Cappadocian and his successor Saint Epiphanios governed the Church of Constantinople in the early sixth century, in the reigns of Justin and Justinian. Both laboured to restore communion with Rome after the Acacian schism.

They reposed in peace and are commemorated together.
8-25.desc: Saints Epiphanios and John the Cappadocian, Archbishops of Constantinople.
8-25.name: Epiphanios and John, Patriarchs of Constantinople

8-25.bio:
Saint Menas was Patriarch of Constantinople in the reign of Justinian the Great, in whose time the Church of Hagia Sophia was built. He presided over the Church in the years before the Fifth Ecumenical Council.

He reposed in peace in the sixth century.
8-25.name: Menas Patriarch of Constantinople

8-25.bio:
Saint Konstantia lived in Paphos in Cyprus and was a devoted disciple of Saint Hilarion the Great, whose relics she guarded after his repose.

She reposed in peace and is honoured among the saints of Cyprus.
8-25.desc: Saint Konstantia of Paphos in Cyprus, disciple of Saint Hilarion the Great.
8-25.name: Konstantia of Paphos

8-26.bio:
Sts. Adrian and Natalia were a married couple of Nicomedia in the time of the persecution of Maximian, at the beginning of the fourth century. Adrian, an imperial official, was so moved by the courage of imprisoned Christians that he confessed Christ and was enrolled among them; his young wife Natalia, secretly a Christian, strengthened him in prison and stood by him through his tortures and martyrdom.

Natalia afterward guarded his memory faithfully and reposed in peace, counted among the confessors. They are commemorated together on August 26 as an image of marriage sanctified by faith.
8-26.name: Adrian and Natalia

8-26.bio:
According to the celebrated tale of Barlaam and Joasaph, Joasaph was a prince of India whose father sought to shield him from all knowledge of suffering and faith. Instructed by the hermit Barlaam, he embraced Christ, later converted his father and finally left his throne for the desert.

He is honoured with Barlaam and Abenner as a model of renunciation.
8-26.desc: Venerable Joasaph, son of King Abenner of India.
8-26.name: Joasaph of India

8-26.bio:
Saint Tithoes was one of the desert fathers of Egypt, a disciple of Saint Pachomios, remembered for his prayer and humility.

He reposed in peace.
8-26.name: Tithoes the Ascetic

8-26.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saints Attikos and Sisinios confessed Christ and were put to death by the sword.

They are commemorated together on this day.
8-26.name: Attikos and Sisinios

8-26.bio:
Blessed Maria lived at the Diveyevo convent in Russia as a fool-for-Christ in the early twentieth century, continuing the line of blessed women of that community. She was known for her gift of foresight and endured the persecutions after the Revolution.

She reposed in 1931 and was glorified together with the other blessed ones of Diveyevo.
8-26.desc: Blessed Maria Ivanovna of Diveyevo, Fool-for-Christ.
8-26.name: Maria of Diveyevo

8-27.bio:
St. Poimen the Great was one of the most renowned of the desert fathers of Egypt, living in the fourth and fifth centuries. With his brothers he took up the monastic life in Sketis, and became a discerning elder to whom monks came from afar for a word of guidance.

More of his sayings are preserved in the Sayings of the Desert Fathers than of any other elder, breathing humility, mercy toward the sinner, and sobriety of soul. His name means shepherd. He reposed at a great age and is commemorated on August 27.
8-27.desc: Venerable Poimen the Great, desert father.
8-27.name: Poimenas the Great

8-27.bio:
St. Phanourios is a Great Martyr whose icon was discovered on the island of Rhodes in the fourteenth century, showing a young soldier surrounded by scenes of his sufferings for Christ. His name means the one who reveals, and nothing of his life is known beyond what the icon itself testifies: that he endured many tortures and gave his life rather than deny his Lord.

He is beloved throughout the Greek world as the revealer of lost things. According to tradition, the faithful bake a phanouropita, a simple spice cake, in his honor when asking his intercession, sharing it with others in remembrance of his mother.
8-27.desc: Holy Great Martyr Phanourios the Newly Revealed of Rhodes.
8-27.name: Phanourios

8-27.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Anthousa the New confessed Christ and was cast into a well for her faith.

She is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-27.desc: Holy Martyr Anthousa the New, drowned in a well for Christ.
8-27.name: Anthousa the New

8-27.bio:
Saint Liberius was bishop of Rome in the fourth century during the Arian controversy. He defended Saint Athanasios the Great and was exiled by the Emperor Constantius for refusing to condemn him.

He was later restored to his see and reposed in peace.
8-27.desc: Saint Liberius the Confessor, Pope of Rome.
8-27.name: Liberius Pope of Rome

8-27.bio:
Saint Hosius was bishop of Cordoba in Spain and adviser to the Emperor Constantine the Great. He presided at the First Ecumenical Council in Nicaea and was a firm defender of the Orthodox faith against Arianism, suffering exile in his old age.

He reposed at a great age in the fourth century.
8-27.desc: Saint Hosius, Bishop of Cordoba in Spain, confessor.
8-27.name: Hosius of Cordoba

8-27.bio:
Arkadios, son of Theodosius the Great, was emperor of the East at the turn of the fifth century. Although his reign saw the exile of Saint John Chrysostom, the Greek synaxaria remember him among the pious emperors.

He reposed in 408.
8-27.desc: Righteous Arkadios, Emperor of the Romans.
8-27.name: Arkadios the Emperor

8-28.bio:
St. Moses the Ethiopian was in his youth a slave and then the leader of a band of robbers in Egypt, feared for his strength and violence. Coming to himself, he repented and entered the monastic life in the desert of Sketis, where through long struggle with his former passions he attained deep humility and gentleness, and was found worthy of the priesthood.

He was killed when barbarians attacked the monastery, having refused to lift a weapon in his own defense. A powerful witness that no sinner is beyond repentance, he is commemorated on August 28.
8-28.desc: Venerable Moses the Ethiopian, desert father.
8-28.name: Moses the Ethiopian

8-28.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saints Diomedes and Lawrence confessed Christ and were put to death for their faith.

They are commemorated together on this day.
8-28.name: Diomedes and Lawrence

8-28.bio:
Hezekiah was king of Judah in the days of the Prophet Isaiah. He cleansed the Temple, destroyed the idols and trusted in God when Jerusalem was besieged by the Assyrians; the Scriptures relate that his prayer was heard and fifteen years were added to his life.

He is honoured among the righteous of the Old Testament.
8-28.name: Hezekiah the King

8-28.bio:
Saint Anna was an aged widow of the tribe of Asher who served God with fasting and prayer in the Temple. The Gospel of Luke relates that she was present when the infant Christ was brought there and spoke of Him to all who awaited the redemption of Jerusalem.

She is honoured with the Righteous Symeon on the feast of the Meeting and again on this day.
8-28.desc: Righteous Anna the Prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, who met the infant Christ in the Temple.
8-28.name: Anna the Prophetess

8-28.bio:
The synaxaria record that thirty-three Christians of Heraclea confessed Christ and were burned for their faith.

They are honoured together as a company.
8-28.desc: Holy Thirty-Three Martyrs who suffered at Heraclea.
8-28.name: Thirty-Three Martyrs of Heraclea

8-28.bio:
On this day the Church honours together the many ascetics whose relics rest in the Far Caves of the Kiev Caves Lavra, founded by Saint Theodosios in the eleventh century.

They are the spiritual fathers of Russian monasticism.
8-28.desc: Synaxis of the Venerable Fathers of the Far Caves of the Kiev Caves Lavra.
8-28.name: Fathers of the Kiev Caves

8-29.bio:
The Church commemorates on August 29 the martyric death of St. John the Forerunner. Imprisoned by Herod Antipas for rebuking his unlawful union with Herodias, John was beheaded at the request of Herodias, made through her daughter, whose dancing had pleased Herod at his birthday feast. Thus the greatest of the prophets sealed his preaching of repentance with his blood.

The day is kept as a strict fast, in sorrow for the deed and in honor of the Forerunner. The faithful remember him as the friend of the Bridegroom, who according to the hymns of the Church preached the coming of Christ even to those in Hades.
8-29.desc: Beheading of the Holy Glorious Prophet and Forerunner John the Baptist.
8-29.name: Beheading of John the Baptist

8-29.bio:
Saint Theodora of Thessaloniki, born on Aegina, lived as a nun in Thessaloniki in the ninth century in humility and obedience. On this day the Church remembers her repose.

Her relics, which streamed fragrant myrrh, are venerated in the city to this day.
8-29.desc: Venerable Theodora of Thessaloniki, myrrh-streaming nun.
8-29.name: Theodora of Thessaloniki

8-29.bio:
Saint Arkadios was bishop of Arsinoe in Cyprus, remembered as a gentle shepherd and a wonderworker.

He reposed in peace and is honoured among the saints of Cyprus.
8-29.desc: Saint Arkadios the Wonderworker, Bishop of Arsinoe in Cyprus.
8-29.name: Arkadios of Arsinoe

8-29.bio:
Basil I rose from humble origins in Macedonia to become emperor in 867 and founded the Macedonian dynasty. The Greek synaxaria remember him for his building of churches, his legal reforms and his care for the Church.

He reposed in 886.
8-29.desc: Righteous Basil the Macedonian, Emperor of the Romans.
8-29.name: Basil the Macedonian

8-29.bio:
Saint Joseph was born in Crete and became a monk, serving as abbot near Heraklion and caring for the poor and the sick. He reposed in the early sixteenth century and his relics were later carried to Zakynthos, where they are venerated.

His principal feast is on the twenty-second of January.
8-29.desc: Venerable Joseph the Sanctified of Samakos in Crete, remembered on the placing of his relics.
8-29.name: Joseph the Sanctified of Samakos

8-3.bio:
St. Phokas the Gardener lived near Sinope on the Black Sea, cultivating a small garden by the city gate and giving freely of its produce to the poor and to travelers, whom he received with open hospitality. In a time of persecution, soldiers were sent to find and kill the Christian Phokas; unknowing, they lodged with him, and he, having prepared his own grave in the night, revealed himself in the morning and received death for Christ.

He has long been honored as a patron of gardeners and of seafarers. He is commemorated on August 3.
8-3.name: Phokas the Gardener

8-3.bio:
Saint Isaakios was the monk who boldly rebuked the Arian emperor Valens and later founded a monastery in Constantinople. Dalmatos, a former officer of the imperial guard, became his disciple and successor, and Dalmatos' son Faustos followed him as abbot.

The monastery, later called the Dalmatos Monastery, became one of the most important in the capital, and its founders are honoured together on this day.
8-3.desc: Venerable Isaakios, Dalmatos and Faustos, ascetics of the Dalmatos Monastery in Constantinople.
8-3.name: Dalmatos, Faustos and Isaakios

8-3.bio:
Salome was the wife of Zebedee and mother of the Apostles James and John. The Gospels count her among the women who followed Christ and ministered to Him, and who went to the tomb with myrrh on the morning of the Resurrection.

She is honoured with the other Myrrhbearing Women and is remembered separately on this day.
8-3.desc: Holy Myrrhbearer Salome, mother of the Apostles James and John.
8-3.name: Salome the Myrrhbearer

8-3.bio:
Saint Theodora was born on the island of Aegina in the ninth century and, after the death of her husband, entered a monastery in Thessaloniki with her daughter Theopiste. Tradition relates that they lived in great obedience and humility, and that Theodora's relics later streamed fragrant myrrh.

She is one of the patron saints of Thessaloniki, where her relics are venerated to this day.
8-3.desc: Venerable Theodora of Aegina and her daughter Theopiste, nuns in Thessaloniki.
8-3.name: Theodora of Aegina and Theopiste

8-3.bio:
Saint Anthony was born in Rome to Orthodox parents and became a monk. Tradition relates that he was miraculously carried across the sea to Novgorod, where he founded a monastery dedicated to the Nativity of the Theotokos.

He reposed in the twelfth century and is honoured as one of the great ascetics of the Russian north.
8-3.desc: Venerable Anthony the Roman, wonderworker and founder of a monastery at Novgorod.
8-3.name: Anthony the Roman of Novgorod

8-3.bio:
Saint Theoklito lived in the Byzantine period as a married laywoman who devoted herself to almsgiving and prayer. Tradition relates that she gave away nearly all she had to the poor and was granted the gift of working miracles.

She reposed in peace and is remembered by the Church as an example of holiness in ordinary life.
8-3.desc: Venerable Theoklito the Wonderworker, a married woman of great charity.
8-3.name: Theoklito the Wonderworker

8-30.bio:
St. Alexander was a martyr of the early Church who confessed Christ before his persecutors and sealed his faith with his blood. The synaxaria preserve little of his life beyond his noble standing and his faithful confession unto death.

His memory is kept among the saints of this day, and those who bear the name Alexander honor him in their prayers. He is commemorated on August 30.
8-30.name: Alexander the Patrician

8-30.bio:
Saint John the Faster served as Patriarch of Constantinople in the sixth century and was renowned for his fasting and almsgiving. Saint Paul the New held the same throne in the eighth century and resigned it in penitence for having served under the iconoclasts.

They are commemorated together with Saint Alexander on this day.
8-30.desc: Saints John and Paul the New, Patriarchs of Constantinople, commemorated with Saint Alexander.
8-30.name: John and Paul the New, Patriarchs of Constantinople

8-30.bio:
Saint Alexander was Prince of Novgorod and later Grand Prince of Vladimir in the thirteenth century. He defended Orthodox Rus against the Swedes and the Teutonic Knights while dealing wisely with the Mongols, and before his death he received the monastic schema.

This day marks the translation of his relics to Saint Petersburg in 1724.
8-30.desc: Right-believing Prince Alexander Nevsky, remembered on the translation of his relics.
8-30.name: Alexander Nevsky

8-30.bio:
Saint Alexander was a monk of Valaam who withdrew to the wilderness by the river Svir, where a monastery grew up around him. Tradition relates that he was granted a vision of the Holy Trinity.

He reposed in 1533 and his relics remain incorrupt.
8-30.desc: Venerable Alexander of Svir, wonderworker of the Russian north.
8-30.name: Alexander of Svir

8-30.bio:
Saint Phantinos was a Greek monk of Calabria in southern Italy who lived in great asceticism and later travelled to Thessaloniki, where he reposed in the tenth century.

He is honoured as a wonderworker.
8-30.desc: Venerable Phantinos the Wonderworker of Calabria.
8-30.name: Phantinos the Wonderworker

8-30.bio:
Saint Vryaine was an ascetic woman who lived in prayer and stillness and reposed in peace.

Little more is preserved of her life.
8-30.desc: Venerable Vryaine, who reposed in peace.
8-30.name: Vryaine the Ascetic

8-30.bio:
Saint Philonides was bishop of Kourion in Cyprus during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that he gave up his soul to God rather than be defiled by his persecutors.

He is honoured among the saints of Cyprus.
8-30.desc: Hieromartyr Philonides, Bishop of Kourion in Cyprus.
8-30.name: Philonides of Kourion

8-31.bio:
St. Aidan was an Irish monk of the monastery of Iona who in the seventh century was sent at the request of King Oswald to evangelize the kingdom of Northumbria in northern England. Consecrated bishop, he made his seat on the island of Lindisfarne, from which he traveled on foot through the countryside, preaching Christ with gentleness, ransoming captives, and giving to the poor whatever he received.

His humility and charity won the hearts of the people, and Lindisfarne became a great center of prayer and mission. He reposed in 651 and is commemorated on August 31.
8-31.name: Aidan of Lindisfarne

8-31.bio:
The Church commemorates the placing of the Belt of the Theotokos in the Church of Chalkoprateia in Constantinople. Tradition relates that the Belt was later laid upon the Empress Zoe, who was healed of a grave illness.

A portion of the Belt is kept today at the Monastery of Vatopedi on Mount Athos.
8-31.desc: Placing of the Honourable Belt of the Most Holy Theotokos in the Church of Chalkoprateia.
8-31.name: Deposition of the Belt of the Theotokos

8-31.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Phileortos confessed Christ and was put to death for his faith.

He is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-31.name: Phileortos the Martyr

8-31.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Diadochos confessed Christ and was beheaded for his faith.

He is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-31.name: Diadochos the Martyr

8-31.bio:
The synaxaria record that seven Christian virgins of Gaza confessed Christ and were put to death for their faith.

They are honoured together as a company.
8-31.desc: Holy Seven Virgin Martyrs of Gaza.
8-31.name: Seven Virgins of Gaza

8-31.bio:
The synaxaria record that three hundred and sixty-six Christians of Nicomedia confessed Christ and were put to death together.

They are honoured as a company on this day.
8-31.desc: Holy Three Hundred and Sixty-Six Martyrs who suffered at Nicomedia.
8-31.name: 366 Martyrs of Nicomedia

8-4.bio:
The Seven Holy Youths of Ephesus were young Christians of noble standing who, during the persecution of the Emperor Decius in the third century, took refuge in a cave outside the city rather than sacrifice to idols. There, by the providence of God, they fell into a wondrous sleep, and the cave was sealed.

Generations later, in the days of the Emperor Theodosius the Younger, they were found alive, a living witness against those who doubted the resurrection of the dead. Having borne this testimony, they reposed in peace. They are commemorated on August 4.
8-4.name: Seven Youths of Ephesus

8-4.bio:
Saint Eudokia, known also as Ia, was a Christian woman taken captive in Persia in the fourth century. Tradition relates that she converted many Persian women to Christ and was tortured and put to death for her faith.

Her relics were later brought to Constantinople, and the translation of her relics is remembered on this day.
8-4.desc: Holy Martyr Eudokia, also called Ia, who suffered in Persia.
8-4.name: Eudokia (Ia) of Persia

8-4.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Thathuel was a Christian who confessed Christ before pagan officials and was hanged from a tree for his faith.

Nothing more is known of his life; he is honoured among the martyrs of this day.
8-4.desc: Holy Martyr Thathuel, who was hanged from a tree for Christ.
8-4.name: Thathuel the Martyr

8-5.bio:
St. Eusignios was a soldier of Antioch who served long years in the Roman armies, and according to tradition had served under Constantine the Great and beheld the appearing of the sign of the Cross. In extreme old age, in the reign of Julian the Apostate, he was denounced as a Christian; brought before the emperor, he boldly rebuked his apostasy and confessed Christ, for which he was beheaded.

His martyrdom in old age crowned a lifetime of faithfulness. He is commemorated on August 5.
8-5.name: Eusignios

8-5.bio:
Saint Nonna was the wife of Gregory of Nazianzus the Elder and the mother of Saint Gregory the Theologian, Saint Caesarius and Saint Gorgonia. Raised a Christian, she brought her husband to the faith and raised her children in piety.

Her son wrote movingly of her prayer and charity; she reposed in peace in the fourth century, shortly after her husband.
8-5.desc: Righteous Nonna, mother of Saint Gregory the Theologian.
8-5.name: Nonna the Righteous

8-5.bio:
Saint Evgenios Giannoulis was born in Aitolia in the seventeenth century and became a hieromonk and scholar. He founded schools in Agrafa and elsewhere, teaching the children of enslaved Greeks the faith and Greek letters.

He is honoured as one of the great teachers of the nation and a forerunner of Saint Kosmas of Aitolia.
8-5.desc: Venerable Evgenios the Aitolian, teacher of the Greek nation under Ottoman rule.
8-5.name: Evgenios of Aitolia

8-5.bio:
Saint Chrestos was a young Greek from Preveza in Epirus who worked in Constantinople. Accused before the Ottoman authorities, he refused to deny Christ and was put to death in the eighteenth century.

He is counted among the New Martyrs of the Turkish yoke.
8-5.desc: Holy New Martyr Chrestos of Preveza, who suffered at Constantinople.
8-5.name: Chrestos of Preveza

8-5.bio:
Saint Euthymios was a monk and spiritual father to Emperor Leo the Wise before being raised to the patriarchal throne of Constantinople in the early tenth century. He was deposed and exiled amid the disputes over the emperor's fourth marriage.

He bore his exile patiently and reposed in a monastery, being honoured by the Church as a confessor.
8-5.desc: Saint Euthymios, Patriarch of Constantinople, confessor.
8-5.name: Euthymios Patriarch of Constantinople

8-5.bio:
Saint John Jacob was a Romanian monk who left for the Holy Land and lived as a hermit in the Judean desert near the Monastery of Saint George of Choziba. He was known for strict asceticism, spiritual writings and gentleness toward all who sought him.

He reposed in 1960 and his relics were found incorrupt; he is honoured throughout the Orthodox world.
8-5.desc: Venerable John Jacob the New Chozebite, Romanian ascetic of the Holy Land.
8-5.name: John the New Chozebite

8-6.bio:
The Great Feast of the Transfiguration commemorates the day Christ led Peter, James, and John up Mount Tabor and was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, His garments became white as light, Moses and Elijah appeared speaking with Him, and the voice of the Father declared Him the beloved Son.

The feast, kept on August 6 in the midst of the Dormition Fast, reveals the uncreated light of the divinity of Christ and the glory to which the human person is called. In Greek tradition the first grapes of the harvest are brought to church on this day to be blessed.
8-6.desc: The Holy Transfiguration of our Lord and God and Saviour Jesus Christ.
8-6.name: Transfiguration of the Lord

8-6.bio:
Saint Abbakoum was a monk from Mount Athos who confessed Christ openly before the Ottoman authorities in Thessaloniki. Tradition relates that he went to his martyrdom with joy on the feast of the Transfiguration.

He is honoured among the New Martyrs of the Church.
8-6.desc: Holy New Martyr Abbakoum, who suffered at Thessaloniki.
8-6.name: Abbakoum the New Martyr

8-7.bio:
St. Dometios was a Persian of the fourth century who came to faith in Christ and left his homeland for the regions of Syria and Mesopotamia, where he received the monastic tonsure and later lived in ascetic solitude, drawing many who sought healing and counsel through his prayers.

In the reign of Julian the Apostate he was put to death for Christ, stoned, according to tradition, together with two disciples. He is commemorated on August 7.
8-7.name: Dometios the Persian

8-7.bio:
Saint Narkissos was bishop of Jerusalem at the end of the second century. Tradition relates that he lived to a very great age, withdrew for a time into the desert after being slandered, and returned to his see to serve alongside Saint Alexander.

He is remembered for a miracle in which water drawn for the Paschal vigil was changed into oil for the lamps.
8-7.desc: Saint Narkissos, Patriarch of Jerusalem and wonderworker.
8-7.name: Narkissos Patriarch of Jerusalem

8-7.bio:
Saint Theodosios was born in Athens in the ninth century and became a monk, settling as a hermit near Argos in the Peloponnese. Many came to him for healing and counsel, and a monastery grew up around his cell.

He is called the Healer because of the cures worked through his prayers, and his relics are venerated in the Argolid.
8-7.desc: Venerable Theodosios the New, healer and ascetic of the Peloponnese.
8-7.name: Theodosios the New of Argos

8-7.bio:
Saint Nikanor was born in Thessaloniki in the fifteenth century and, after distributing his wealth to the poor, embraced the monastic life. He founded the Monastery of the Transfiguration at Zavorda on Mount Kallistratos in western Macedonia.

He is greatly venerated in Macedonia, where his relics are kept, and is known as a wonderworker.
8-7.desc: Venerable Nikanor the Wonderworker, founder of the Monastery of Zavorda on Mount Kallistratos.
8-7.name: Nikanor of Zavorda

8-7.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Potamia was a virgin who confessed Christ and was beheaded by the sword.

She is called Wonderworker because of the miracles attributed to her intercessions.
8-7.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Potamia the Wonderworker.
8-7.name: Potamia the Wonderworker

8-7.bio:
Saint Asterios was a Roman senator who, tradition relates, reverently buried the body of the martyr Marinos at Caesarea in Palestine. For this act of faith he was himself arrested and beheaded in the third century.

He is honoured among the martyrs of Caesarea.
8-7.desc: Holy Martyr Asterios the Senator, who suffered at Caesarea in Palestine.
8-7.name: Asterios the Senator

8-7.bio:
Saint Theodora was born in Moldavia in the seventeenth century and, after her marriage was dissolved by agreement, became a nun. She lived for many years as a hermitess in a cave near the Sihla skete, enduring cold and hunger in prayer.

Tradition relates that birds brought her food in her last years; she is one of the most beloved women saints of Romania.
8-7.desc: Venerable Theodora of Sihla, hermitess of the Carpathian mountains.
8-7.name: Theodora of Sihla

8-8.bio:
St. Emilian was bishop of Cyzicus in the ninth century, during the renewed persecution of the holy icons. Summoned to reject the veneration of the icons of Christ and the saints, he refused, defending the Orthodox faith with firmness before the iconoclast emperor.

For his confession he was driven from his see and endured exile and hardship until his blessed repose, receiving the title of Confessor from the Church he would not betray. He is commemorated on August 8.
8-8.name: Emilian the Confessor

8-8.bio:
Saint Myron was a farmer of Crete known for his generosity, who was later ordained and became bishop of Gortyna. Tradition relates that he once caught thieves in his threshing floor and helped them carry away the grain, moving them to repentance.

He reposed in old age in the fourth century and is honoured as a wonderworker.
8-8.desc: Saint Myron the Wonderworker, Bishop of Crete.
8-8.name: Myron of Crete (Bishop)

8-8.bio:
Saint Triantaphyllos was a young sailor from Zagora on Mount Pelion. Accused before the Ottoman authorities in Constantinople, he refused to renounce Christ despite threats and flattery and was beheaded in the seventeenth century.

He is one of the New Martyrs of the Turkish yoke and the patron of all who bear his name.
8-8.desc: Holy New Martyr Triantaphyllos of Zagora, who suffered at Constantinople.
8-8.name: Triantaphyllos of Zagora

8-8.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saints Eleutherios and Leonides, together with a number of children, were cast into a fire for confessing Christ.

They are honoured together on this day.
8-8.desc: Holy Martyrs Eleutherios, Leonides and the Holy Infants, burned for Christ.
8-8.name: Eleutherios and Leonides

8-8.bio:
Saint Kallinikos Poulos was Metropolitan of Edessa in northern Greece in the twentieth century, remembered for his simplicity of life, pastoral zeal and love for the poor. He reposed in 1984.

He was numbered among the saints by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2020.
8-8.desc: Saint Kallinikos, Metropolitan of Edessa, Pella and Almopia.
8-8.name: Kallinikos of Edessa

8-8.bio:
Saint Anastasios was a young Bulgarian who worked in Thessaloniki. Tradition relates that he was pressured to accept Islam, repented of a moment of weakness and confessed Christ before the Ottoman judge, for which he was put to death in the eighteenth century.

He is honoured among the New Martyrs.
8-8.desc: Holy New Martyr Anastasios of Bulgaria, who suffered at Thessaloniki.
8-8.name: Anastasios of Bulgaria

8-9.bio:
St. Matthias was a disciple of the Lord from the beginning, one of those who accompanied Him from the baptism of John until the Ascension. After the fall of Judas, the Apostles prayed and cast lots, and Matthias was chosen to take his place among the Twelve, as recorded in the Acts of the Apostles.

According to tradition he preached the Gospel with boldness and completed his apostolic course as a martyr. He is commemorated on August 9.
8-9.desc: Holy Apostle Matthias chosen to replace Judas.
8-9.name: Matthias the Apostle

8-9.bio:
During the persecution of the iconoclast emperor Leo the Isaurian, a group of Christians resisted the removal of the icon of Christ from the Chalke Gate of the imperial palace. Ten of them, including women, were imprisoned and put to death.

They are honoured as martyrs and confessors of the holy icons.
8-9.desc: Holy Ten Martyrs who suffered for the holy icons at the Chalke Gate of Constantinople.
8-9.name: Ten Martyrs of Chalke

8-9.bio:
The synaxaria record that Saint Antoninos confessed Christ in Alexandria and was burned alive for his faith.

He is commemorated among the martyrs of this day.
8-9.desc: Holy Martyr Antoninos of Alexandria, who was burned for Christ.
8-9.name: Antoninos of Alexandria

8-9.bio:
Saint Herman was a monk of Valaam who went with the first Orthodox mission to Alaska in 1794. He settled on Spruce Island, where he cared for orphans, defended the native Aleuts against the abuses of traders and lived in prayer and simplicity.

He reposed in 1837 and was glorified in 1970 as the first saint of Orthodox America.
8-9.desc: Venerable Herman of Alaska, wonderworker and enlightener of the Aleuts.
8-9.name: Herman of Alaska

8-9.bio:
Saint Euthymios was Metropolitan of Rhodes in the seventeenth century. Tradition relates that he was imprisoned and tormented by the Ottoman authorities for his defence of his flock and died in confinement.

He is honoured by the Church of Rhodes as a hieromartyr.
8-9.name: Euthymios of Rhodes

8-9.bio:
Saint Psoes was one of the desert fathers of Egypt, who lived in asceticism and reposed in peace.

Little is recorded of his life beyond his name and his place among the venerable ascetics.
8-9.desc: Venerable Psoes, ascetic of the Egyptian desert.
8-9.name: Psoes of Egypt
